chunks.title: Muscle actions & the laws
chunks.tldr: ~4% of children have strabismus. Tropia = manifest; phoria = latent (only when fusion broken). Actions: MR adduct, LR abduct; SR elevate/intort/adduct; IR depress/extort/adduct; SO intort/depress/abduct; IO extort/elevate/abduct. Vertical recti act most in abduction; obliques in adduction. Sherrington: agonist contracts, antagonist relaxes. Hering: yoke muscles get equal innervation (R gaze = RLR + LMR; up-right = RSR + LIO; down-right = RIR + LSO). Infant alignment normal by 2–3 months.
points: Secondary deviation (paretic eye fixing) > primary (Hering's law overshoot).
Positive angle kappa looks exotropic; negative looks esotropic.

cards.a: Yoke muscles (agonists moving both eyes the same way) receive equal and simultaneous innervation.

cards.q: Why is secondary deviation larger than primary in a palsy?
cards.a: The paretic eye fixing needs extra innervation, which is also sent to its yoke muscle (Hering), causing overshoot.

chunks.title: Sensory adaptations & amblyopia
chunks.tldr: Binocular vision: corresponding points, Panum's area, sensory fusion, stereopsis (~60 arc-sec needs bifoveal fixation). Strabismus before age ~7–8 → suppression (facultative; esotropia elliptical, exotropia whole temporal hemiretina), ARC (extrafoveal point acts as fovea, binocular only), amblyopia, eccentric fixation (monocular). After that age → diplopia (confusion rarely). Amblyopia: VA loss beyond structural cause from abnormal input <7 y — strabismic (esotropia worse; alternators spared), anisometropic, deprivation (cataract, ptosis).

cards.a: Suppression is present only under binocular viewing; amblyopia persists when the eye is tested alone.

cards.q: Why do alternating strabismics not get amblyopia?
cards.a: Each eye takes turns fixing, so both visual pathways get foveal stimulation.

chunks.title: Strabismus examination
chunks.tldr: History (onset, constant/intermittent, family, prematurity, neuro). VA (age-appropriate), cycloplegic refraction, dilated fundus (RB, ONH hypoplasia, glioma can present as squint). Cover test → tropia (eye moves out to fix = esotropia). Uncover → phoria/fixation preference. Alternate cover → total deviation. Prism + alternate cover quantifies (apex toward deviation; don't stack). Hirschberg: ~18 PD per mm (some use 7°/mm) light reflex decentration; Krimsky: prism centres reflex. Ductions/versions in 9 gazes, NPC (≤5 cm normal), AC/A (~6 PD/D). Sensory: Titmus/Frisby/TNO stereo, Worth 4-dot, red filter.
points: Pseudoesotropia: broad nasal bridge/epicanthus with centred light reflexes — outgrows.
chunks.hook: Cover the fixing eye — watch what the other one does.

cards.q: On cover test, the uncovered eye moves outward to take up fixation. Diagnosis?

cards.a: About 6 prism dioptres per dioptre of accommodation (≈ IPD in cm).

chunks.title: Amblyopia treatment & non-surgical options
chunks.tldr: Treat as soon as found; best before 7–8 y; align eyes ideally by age 2. Glasses first (full hyperopic correction in esotropia). Occlusion 2–14 h/day (gold standard; full-time max ~1 week per year of age to avoid reverse amblyopia). Atropine penalisation of the good eye (works if good eye hyperopic/emmetropic). Maintenance tapering until 5–13 y. Prisms (Fresnel; ground-in ≤8–10 PD/lens), prism adaptation test. Botulinum into a muscle (temporary, can shift balance). Orthoptic exercises for convergence insufficiency.

cards.a: When the better eye is emmetropic or hyperopic (atropine blurs its near vision).

chunks.title: Strabismus surgery
chunks.tldr: Weaken: recession (rectus), SO tenotomy/lengthening, IO myectomy/recession/anterior transposition (DVD). Strengthen: resection, tuck/plication. Redirect: vertical recti transposition to LR (VI palsy), vertical shift of horizontal recti for A/V patterns (MR toward apex, LR toward open end), Harada-Ito (anterior SO fibres → intorsion). Faden posterior fixation weakens in field of action only. MRs affect near more, LRs distance more. Adjustable sutures for adults/reoperations.
chunks.hook: Recess to weaken, resect to strengthen, transpose to redirect.

cards.q: What does the Harada-Ito procedure correct?
cards.a: Excyclotorsion (e.g. bilateral SO palsy) by tightening the anterior superior oblique fibres.

chunks.title: Infantile & accommodative esotropia
chunks.tldr: Infantile: onset ≤6 mo, large (≥40 PD), comitant, cross-fixation, little refractive error, abduction looks limited (doll's head normal); later DVD, IO overaction, latent nystagmus. Rx: amblyopia treatment, trial glasses if >+3 D, then early bilateral MR recession (or R&R). Accommodative (2–3 y): refractive — high hyperopia; full cycloplegic correction straightens. High AC/A — eso greater at near; glasses + bifocals (or miotics). Partially accommodative: operate on residual. Acquired non-accommodative: consider neuroimaging (posterior fossa).
points: ≥50% of infantile ET later develop an accommodative component.
chunks.hook: Toddler crossing more when looking at books = high AC/A → bifocals.

cards.q: Typical age and treatment of refractive accommodative esotropia?
cards.a: 2–3 years; full cycloplegic hyperopic spectacle correction.

cards.q: Associated findings that develop later in infantile esotropia?
cards.a: Dissociated vertical deviation, inferior oblique overaction, latent/manifest-latent nystagmus.

chunks.title: Sixth nerve palsy
chunks.tldr: Incomitant esotropia: worse at distance, on gaze to the affected side, and with affected eye fixing; head turn toward palsy. Adults: microvascular (diabetes/HTN, recovers ~3 months); also raised ICP (false localising), tumour, trauma, inflammation — image if young, other signs or no recovery. Rx: occlusion/prism ± botox to ipsilateral MR; after 6 months: partial → MR recession + LR resection; complete → vertical rectus transposition (± MR botox). Children: watch for amblyopia. Other ET causes: medial wall fracture, thyroid MR, Duane.
chunks.hook: Worse at distance and toward the bad side = lateral rectus problem.

cards.q: Surgery for complete VI palsy after 6 months?
cards.a: Transposition of the vertical rectus muscles toward the lateral rectus (± MR botulinum or recession).

chunks.title: Exotropia
chunks.tldr: Types by distance vs near: basic, divergence excess (distance > near), pseudo-divergence excess (+3 lens equalises), convergence insufficiency (near > distance). Intermittent XT: >half of exotropia, by 5 y; drifts at distance, when tired; closes one eye in bright light; amblyopia rare. Rx: correct refraction, minus lenses/part-time patching to delay; surgery when control deteriorates — bilateral LR recession (distance) or R&R (near); aim slight overcorrection. Constant XT: infantile → neuro assessment; sensory exotropia from a poorly seeing eye (adults).
chunks.hook: Child squinting one eye in the sunshine = intermittent exotropia.

cards.q: Classic sign of intermittent exotropia in children?
cards.a: Closing one eye in bright sunlight; deviation appears at distance or when tired.

chunks.title: A/V patterns & vertical deviations
chunks.tldr: V pattern = more exo/less eso in upgaze (IO overaction); A pattern = more eso/less exo in upgaze (SO overaction). Treat oblique overaction, or shift horizontal insertions half–one tendon width. Hypertropia named by the higher eye. Causes: congenital SO palsy (large vertical fusional amplitudes, old photos show head tilt), trauma (IV), orbital floor fracture (IR entrapment), thyroid (IR fibrosis), skew, MG, MS. Parks 3-step: which eye higher → worse in which gaze → worse with which head tilt (Bielschowsky). RSO palsy: R hyper, worse on left gaze, worse on right tilt; head tilts left. Double Maddox rod measures torsion (SO palsy excyclotorsion; >10° suggests bilateral).
points: Skew deviation: supranuclear, conjugate torsion (higher eye intorts) — brainstem/cerebellum.
chunks.hook: SO palsy: head tilts AWAY from the bad eye.

cards.q: Three-step test result for right superior oblique palsy?
cards.a: Right hypertropia, worse on left gaze, worse on right head tilt.

cards.q: Which overacting muscle causes a V pattern?

chunks.title: Duane, DVD, Brown & heterophoria
chunks.tldr: Duane: congenital cranial dysinnervation — absent VI nucleus, LR innervated by III; limited abduction, globe retraction + fissure narrowing on adduction, up/downshoots; left eye, girls; associations Goldenhar, Klippel-Feil. Surgery for primary position deviation/head turn (MR recession, transposition). DVD: covered eye floats up + extorts, breaks Hering's law; with infantile ET; SR recession ± Faden, IO anterior transposition. Brown: SO tendon/trochlea restriction → can't elevate in adduction, positive forced duction; SO tenotomy/spacer if head posture. Heterophoria: treat only if symptomatic (asthenopia): refraction, plus lenses for eso, prisms (⅓–½ deviation), botox, surgery.
points: Normal fusional vergence at distance: convergence ~14 PD, divergence ~6, vertical ~2.5.
chunks.hook: Duane: eye sinks in and the lids close when it turns in.

cards.a: Absent/hypoplastic abducens nerve with aberrant innervation of the lateral rectus by the oculomotor nerve → co-contraction on adduction.

cards.q: Hallmark motility finding of Brown syndrome?
cards.a: Limited elevation in adduction with positive forced duction test (restrictive).
